subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest model should OpenClaw adopt for stored gateway, channel, and provider secrets: native OS keychain, master-passphrase sealing, SecretRef-only migration, or another security-approved design?
rationale: Automation should not choose key custody, unattended startup, migration, recovery, downgrade, and provider-compatibility behavior for credential storage without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Design native encrypted credential storage
options.body: Define a supported keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus SQLite auth profiles.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs as the mitigation
options.body: Declare transparent encrypted-at-rest storage out of scope and narrow the work to docs, audit, and migration guidance for SecretRefs.

options.title: Use partial sealing as a stepping stone
options.body: Continue the open auth-store sealing work experimentally while leaving this issue open for openclaw.json, backups, SQLite, and migration coverage.

recommendation.title: Design native encrypted credential storage
recommendation.body: Define a supported keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus SQLite auth profiles.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is listed for Security/Agents and authored the overlapping credential-sealing PR, making them the best current routing candidate for the security-boundary decision.
